questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to the us.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Without doubt one of the best experiences of my life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: NC State were very helpful and easy to get in touch with about any questions - both over phone, mail and whatsapp. There are quite a few online portals to navigate, but it's alright and they don't expect you to understand it anyways, so not a problem.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had orientation with all exchange students for the spring semester the first days, and they we were set free. They helped me find the way to my on campus accommodation after arriving, which was great.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We could have had some 'follow-up' orientation, also to keep meeting all the exchange students, but it wasn't needed necessarily.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms and apartments - both shared and individual.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I did have a kitchen in my on campus apartments, but my American roommates were very messy and the kitchen was basically unusable. I picked a mealplan, which was more expensive, but very easy and decent food quality. There's plenty of food options on campus, but not a lot on south/centennial campus, where I lived. For some reason, there's no grocery store close to Wolf Ridge apartments, where I stayed, so you pretty much need a car to buy stuff.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I strongly recommend living on campus, but maybe find somewhere else than Wolf Ridge Apartments - it's not great for exchange students, but it's alright. We were a group of 8 exchange students living there, in different apartments, so we stuck together and helped each other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit confusing, since there's so many options, but it was alright and the Study Abroad Office were very helpful over mail also.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There a course catalog, with all options available, from where you pick your courses. There's an online portal for applying for courses, but I believe we were sent a google form to fill out and the Study Abroad Office took care of everything for us.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Study Abroad Office are great!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take time to look through the available classes, cause there a lot!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Computer Science department is very good, and I had good professors and interesting courses in general I'd say.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 9 credit hours, which is the minimum, and it was good. A bit more work than I expected actually, but about the same as home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I think the style of teaching is somewhere between high school and uni back home in DK, and it depends a lot on the professor. Some professors just do lectures, which I prefer, but others like to ask a lot of questions for the students to discuss and answer - so there's a bit of everything.

There's not really any way to know the style of the professor besides writing them and asking, so I didn't know anything before.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: CSC 414 Foundations of Cryptography, CSC 515 Software Security, CSC 574 Computer and Network Security.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I especially liked the CSC 574 because of the professor Brad Reeves. CSC 414 were very interesting as well, but quite heavy on proofs and math.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No big surprises.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The university health insurance is insanely expensive, so get a good travel insurance from DK - it's way cheaper and then you can get the university insurance waived. On the other hand all public transportation, which is not a lot tbh, is free.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are so many options you won't believe it. There a page with all 600+ clubs/organizations listed, so just reach out and you'll be good.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was part of their Sailing Race team, which was awesome! Also I was somewhat part of their Hacking club and I did different Intermural Sports - like beach volley and soccer.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you enjoy sailing definitely reach out to the Sailpack! They have practice multiple times a week, you get to travel around and compete against other universities, and you even have access to their boats whenever you want and they're not used. Also, the team has a great energy, the coach is awesome and it's a great way to meet some cool Americans.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Honestly, there's not a lot of touristy stuff to see in Raleigh, but it's not too long of a drive to National Parks, big Cities, the Ocean, the Mountains etc. I actually think Raleigh is very well placed for being on exchange and getting around the east coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, it's not that different from DK. However, there's a lot of small differences. The us, and especially the southern states, are very car dependent you'll find. The food is fine, but also very american.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Reach out to the other exchange students as much as possible! Everyone is there alone and want to make friends, so it's a great way to build a social network. For meeting americans I'd recommend joining clubs and organizations.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It's definitely frustrating that the us is so dependent on having a car, but the americans are often nice and drive you around, or you find alternatives with the other exchange students.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love how many resources are put into the clubs and organizations, and how engaged the students are. It creates an awesome campus environment and opens up for a lot of great opportunities and meeting people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Reach out to the other exchange students as much as possible.
Don't do too many credit hours/courses, so you'll have free time.
Get a travel insurance from DK instead of the university one.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The visa applications process is a bit of a headache, but it's alright. Just make sure you don't start too late getting the papers in order.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have met some amazing people, both from Europe and USA, that I hope to keep in touch with. It's such a privilege getting the opportunity to go on exchange and it'll change you as a person. You learn new parts of yourself and get a completely new perspective of the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The feeling of being alone in another country in the beginning is something else that I'd ever experienced before. But reach out and you'll find everyone feels the same.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Even though there's a lot of (paper)work going on exchange, especially outside Europe, it's so worth it. Look forward to the time of your life, and I wish you a great stay!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
